user_decision.question: after/ftplugin/typst.lua, docs/TYPST.md, docs/MAPPINGS.md, and lua/neotex/util/README.md already carry a substantial, unrelated, uncommitted keymap-renaming diff (continuing task 519's <leader>al theme into typst/latex/slidev, plus an unrelated surround-vocabulary rewrite in docs/TYPST.md) that task 248's Phase 2-5 edits must land on top of. Since this repo's commit pipeline stages whole files (not hunks), how should that pre-existing diff be handled before task 248 continues, so its own commits are not swept into task 248's phase history?
options: Commit the pre-existing diff first as its own separate, non-task-248 commit, then resume task 248 Phases 2-5 cleanly on top
Stash the pre-existing diff, implement Phases 2-5 against clean HEAD content, commit task 248's work, then pop the stash back (may need manual conflict resolution against overlapping functions)
Accept mixed commits for Phases 2-5 with an honest disclosure line in the commit body naming the carried unrelated diff, overriding the plan's 'never commit them mixed in' Risk mitigation
Discard the pre-existing uncommitted diff and implement Phases 2-5 from a clean file, accepting the loss of that in-progress renaming/surround work
user_decision.recommended: Commit the pre-existing diff first as its own separate, non-task-248 commit, then resume task 248 Phases 2-5 cleanly on top

next_steps: Resolve the user_decision above, then resume /implement 248 (or /orchestrate 248 --implement) from Phase 2. Phase 1 is committed and does not need to be redone.
